canonical_name: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP, RFC 821 generation)

standardized.notes: RFC 821 publication generation; RFC 788 is the immediately prior SMTP specification.

roles: transfer and relay mail between message transfer agents over reliable ordered data-stream services
addressing: Mail envelope paths/mailboxes and host naming are application-level identifiers; DNS/MX routing intersects later as a separate lineage.
routing_or_forwarding: Supports mail relaying across transport-service environments through intermediate SMTP servers.
error_control: Uses command/reply transaction semantics over a reliable ordered data stream; delivery failures are represented at mail-transfer/application level.

operations.monitoring: Mail queues, relay logs and SMTP replies become key operational artifacts.
operations.diagnostics: MAIL/RCPT/DATA transactions and numeric reply codes expose transfer state.
operations.failure_behavior: Recipients may be accepted/rejected individually; queued relays and error returns are implementation-dependent.

survival.provenance_notes: SMTP descendants remain central to Internet mail; this record is specifically the RFC 821 generation.

open_questions: Trace NCP/TCP/X.25 transport appendices and actual deployed transitions.
Recover early SMTP MTA source code and queue formats.

sources.locator: RFC 821, Introduction and SMTP model/procedure sections

supports: RFC 788 predecessor and formal replacement of RFC 772/780

related_artifacts.notes: SMTP RFC 788/821 replaces MTP RFC 772 lineage.
ESMTP retains SMTP transfer semantics while adding extension negotiation.

notes: SMTP transport should remain distinct from message-format (RFC 822/MIME) and mailbox-access (POP/IMAP) genealogies.
